issues.title: 🚀 GitHub Action + publish to the Marketplace
issues.body:
## Idea
One step in a profile repo and the black hole regenerates itself every day:

```yaml
- uses: FelipeBeltranING/commit-horizon@v1
  with:
    github_user_name: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
    output: dist/commit-horizon.svg
    # theme: color        # or bw
    # mode: disk          # or languages
```

## Where to start
- `action.yml` at the root with `runs.using: node24` and inputs that mirror the CLI flags (`theme`, `mode`, `style`, `langs`, `exclude`, `timezone`, `output`).
- `src/action.js`: read the inputs from `INPUT_*` env vars, reuse `fetchUserData`, `fetchLanguages`, `withIcons` and `renderSVG`. No new dependencies.
- `github.token` is enough for GraphQL, so the Action always gets exact counts.
- An `examples/commit-horizon.yml` workflow that publishes to an `output` branch.

## Done when
- [ ] `action.yml` + `src/action.js` with a test for the input parsing
- [ ] Example workflow in `examples/`
- [ ] README section "Put a black hole in your README (2 minutes)"
- [ ] `v1` tag and Marketplace listing

issues.title: 🌐 Web generator: type a username, see your black hole
issues.body: ## Idea No setup at all: a page where you type your username, pick theme and mode, watch the hole live and copy one Markdown line: ```md ![My black hole](https:///api/hole?user=your-username&mode=languages) ``` ## Where to start - `api/hole.js` (Vercel function): validate the query, call the same pipeline as `scripts/preview.js`, answer `image/svg+xml` with `Cache-Control: s-maxage=14400`. - `public/index.html` + `public/app.js`: input, theme/mode/style pickers, live `` preview and a copy button. - Optional `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var for higher limits. ## Done when - [ ] `/api/hole` with tests for bad input (invalid user, unknown theme) - [ ] Page works on mobile - [ ] README links to the live generator

issues.title: 🎞️ Record the black hole as MP4/GIF for sharing
issues.body:
Animated SVGs don't play on Reddit, X or Discord. A small recorder would let people share their black hole anywhere.

## Where to start
- `tools/record.mjs`: open the SVG in headless Chromium (Playwright, dev dependency only), take N frames with `page.screenshot`, pipe them to ffmpeg.
- The longest orbit sets the loop length: pick `--seconds` so the inner disk does at least one full turn.

## Done when
- [ ] `node tools/record.mjs out/me.svg --out me.mp4` (and `.gif`) with `--fps`, `--width`, `--seconds`
- [ ] README section "Share it as a video"

issues.title: 📏 Calibrate the disk for quieter years
issues.body:
With real data (≈800 contributions, ≈110 active days) the disk looks much thinner and fainter than the demo, which is tuned for a very busy year. Quieter years should still look like a proper black hole.

## Ideas
- Scale the base dust (`fill-opacity="0.12"` for empty days in `src/render.js`) and the haze with `activeDays / 365`.
- Give every active day a minimum size so a 1-contribution day is still visible at README size.
- Compare side by side with `npm run preview` and `?user=` for a quiet, an average and a very busy account.

## Done when
- [ ] Before/after screenshots for 3 real accounts in the PR
- [ ] The demo still looks the same (or better)

issues.title: 🌗 Transparent background for light-mode READMEs
issues.body:
On a light README the dark card is fine, but some people want the black hole floating on their own background.

## Steps
1. Add `--background space|transparent` to `bin/commit-horizon.js` (default `space`).
2. In `src/render.js`, skip the `url(#bg)` rect when it's `transparent`, and switch the labels to a mid-gray that reads on both themes.
3. Add a test in `test/render.test.js` and preview it on the light card of `npm run preview`.

issues.title: 🌙 Moons for your streaks
issues.body:
## Idea
Every 7 days of **current** streak, a small moon joins the orbit (up to 5). If the streak breaks, the moons are gone… and the longest streak of the year leaves a faint ring where they used to be.

| Current streak | Sky |
| --- | --- |
| 7 days | 🌙 one moon |
| 14 days | 🌙🌙 two moons |
| 35+ days | 🌙 × 5, the outer one with a tiny crater |

## Where to start
- `src/stats.js`: `moonsFor(currentStreak)` with a test.
- Draw them with the same front/back trick as the language logos in `src/planets.js` so they pass behind the shadow.

## Done when
- [ ] Moons appear only past each threshold
- [ ] They pass behind the hole on the far side
- [ ] README table updated

issues.title: ☄️ Comets for your merged pull requests
issues.body:
## Idea
Each PR merged in the last 30 days is a comet that dives towards the hole with a tail pointing away from it. PRs to **other people's repos** come from farther away (longer, slower dive).

## Where to start
- GraphQL: `pullRequests(states: MERGED, last: 20)` with `mergedAt` and `repository.owner.login` (token path only; without a token, skip the comets).
- Render: a `<path>` tail with a linear gradient + a head, animated along an ellipse with `offset-path`… or with the same X/Y sine trick used in `src/planets.js` if `offset-path` misbehaves on GitHub.
- Cap at 8 comets to keep the SVG small.

## Done when
- [ ] Comets with own vs. external PRs
- [ ] Test with a fake GraphQL response
- [ ] SVG stays under 300 KB

issues.title: 💥 Supernova on your best day
issues.body:
Today the best day gets a pulsing flare. Make it **explode** once per loop: a bright flash, an expanding shock ring and a slowly fading remnant, then back to the flare.

## Steps
1. In `src/render.js`, next to the `flare` circle, add a ring with a `@keyframes nova` that scales from 1 to ~6 and fades out (≈1 s out of a 12 s loop).
2. Keep it on the same rotating `<g class="o">` so it follows the orbit.
3. Test: one and only one supernova per SVG.

issues.title: 📡 Pulsar for night owls
issues.body:
If most of your commits happen at night (20:00–05:00 in your `--timezone`), a pulsar appears in a corner of the sky, sweeping two thin beams like a lighthouse.

## Where to start
- Commit hours need GraphQL (`contributionsCollection.commitContributionsByRepository` → commits with `committedDate`). Sample the last 100 commits, that's enough.
- Beams: two thin triangles with a radial gradient rotating with `@keyframes spin`.

issues.title: 🛰️ Voyager probe: days since your first commit
issues.body:
A tiny probe drifts slowly across the top of the sky with a label like `VOYAGER · 1,204 days out`.

## Steps
1. Get the account creation date (`createdAt` in GraphQL, `created_at` in REST) in `src/github.js`.
2. In `src/render.js`, draw a small probe (a few `<rect>`s and a dish) that translates from left to right in ~60 s.
3. Hide it if the label would collide with the stats in the corners.
4. Test the day count with a fixed date.

issues.title: ✨ Constellations from your most starred repos
issues.body:
The background stars are random today. Turn your 3–5 most starred repos into small constellations: one bright star per repo (brightness = stars), joined by faint lines, with the repo name on hover-less tiny text.

Keep them out of the corners where the labels live (`inLabel` in `src/render.js`).

issues.title: 🌌 Galaxy mode: one spiral arm per month
issues.body:
## Idea
`--mode galaxy`: no black hole, a face-on spiral galaxy. Each month is an arm, each day a star on it, your busiest month the brightest arm, and the core glows with your current streak.

## Where to start
- New `src/galaxy.js` exporting `renderGalaxy(data, opts)`; reuse `computeStats`, the PRNG and the themes.
- Logarithmic spiral: `r = a·e^(bθ)`, 12 arms offset by 30°.
- The whole galaxy rotates slowly (one `<g>` with `@keyframes spin`).

## Done when
- [ ] `--mode galaxy` in the CLI and the preview
- [ ] Deterministic, script-free and < 300 KB (same tests as the disk)

issues.title: ☀️ Solar system mode: your repos as planets
issues.body: `--mode solar`: a star in the middle (size = yearly total), and your top repos as planets — size by commits this year, color by main language, a ring for repos with stars, moons for open PRs.

issues.title: 🕳️🕳️ Binary black holes: two users merging
issues.body:
## Idea
`--users alice,bob`: two black holes orbiting each other, each with its own disk, spiraling closer the more days you both contributed. Made for pair programmers, teams and study groups (semilleros 🎓).

## Notes
- Two disks at half scale, the barycenter weighted by yearly totals.
- Shared active days could light up a bridge of matter between the two holes.

issues.title: 🔤 Logos for more languages
issues.body:
`DEVICON_SLUGS` in `src/icons.js` maps GitHub language names to devicon folders. Languages that aren't there fall back to initials.

## Steps
1. Check which of these exist in devicon: Nim, Gleam, Solidity, Elm, OCaml, Crystal, Perl, Groovy, Fortran, COBOL, Nix, Terraform (HCL).
2. Add them to `DEVICON_SLUGS` (and to `LINGUIST_COLORS` in `src/languages.js` with their GitHub color).
3. Preview: `node bin/commit-horizon.js --demo --mode languages --out out/x.svg` after editing `demoLanguages` locally.
4. Add a test that every slug in the map resolves to a file when devicon is installed (skip if it isn't).

issues.title: 🌑 Make dark logos readable in orbit (Rust, Shell, Lua, Assembly, Zig)
issues.body:
Dark logos get a faint white halo (`LIGHT_CORE` in `src/planets.js`), but nobody checked them at real README size yet.

## Steps
1. Render a demo with those languages and open it at 100% width on a dark README.
2. Tune the halo (`#lh` gradient) or add a thin light stroke so each logo reads clearly.
3. Attach before/after screenshots to the PR.

issues.title: 🇪🇸 Spanish labels inside the SVG
issues.body:
Add `--locale en|es` (default `en`) so the texts in the SVG can be in Spanish: `CONTRIBUCIONES CAYENDO · ÚLTIMOS 12 MESES`, `racha 9d · más larga 12d · mejor 18 oct (61)`.

## Steps
1. Move the label strings in `src/render.js` to a small `TEXTS = { en: {...}, es: {...} }` object (months included).
2. Wire the flag in `bin/commit-horizon.js` and `?locale=` in `scripts/preview.js`.
3. Test that `es` renders the Spanish strings and escapes them.
